bullets.title: ORCL: Massive Q1 Beat — $30B+ AI Cloud Bookings, RPO Surges to $664B, FY Guidance Raised
bullets.body: Oracle reported Q1 EPS $1.92 vs consensus $1.74 and revenue $19.35B vs $19.14B, with cloud revenue up 60%+. The company booked $30B+ in new AI cloud contracts, lifting RPO $209B y/y to $664B, and delivered 300K+ GPUs (3x Q4 capacity). FY27 guidance raised to $90B+ revenue and $8.10 EPS; Q2 cloud revenue guided +65-71% in constant currency. Stock up ~7% after hours.

bullets.title: ADBE: Q3 Beat, FY Guidance Raised; AI-First ARR >$650M Growing 150%+ YoY
bullets.body: Adobe posted Q3 EPS $6.13 vs $6.08 consensus and revenue $6.76B vs $6.69B. FY revenue guidance raised to $26.576-26.626B and EPS to $24.45-24.50. Total ARR $27.50B (+11.2% YoY); AI-first ARR exceeds $650M growing 150%+ YoY. Q4 guidance slightly below consensus at $6.80-6.85B revenue. Stock +17.6% since June 11.

bullets.title: RH: Massive Margin Beat in Q2; Q4 Guide +16-21% Revenue Growth on Backlog & Estates
bullets.body: Restoration Hardware posted Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin 19.4% vs SA estimate 12.8%, and gross margin 48.2% vs FactSet 43.3%, on revenue $922.2M (+2.6% y/y, beat). Raised FY guidance to +5.5-7.0% revenue growth. Q4 guided +16.1-21.2% revenue with 19.7-22.9% EBITDA margin; backlog adds 6.5pts and RH Estates 8pts. Stock up ~7% after hours; international expansion is a ~340bps EBITDA margin drag.

bullets.title: ANET: Raises 2026 Revenue Guide to $12.6B (+40%); Multi-Year AI Cycle with Scale-Up Revenue in 2028
bullets.body: Arista raised 2026 revenue guidance to ~$12.6B representing 40% growth at the Citi TMT Conference. Purchase commitments tripled to $9.6B over three quarters; supply secured through 2027. Scale-across currently ~1/3 of AI sales; scale-up pilots expected 2027 with commercial revenue in 2028. Citi maintains Buy at $215 PT (13.8% upside, 36x 2028E EPS). Campus targeted to grow from ~$825M to $1.25B in 2026.

bullets.title: DELL: Citi Bull Case — $61B Q2 AI Orders, Enterprise AI Customer Base Up 60%, Only 10-15% Penetrated
bullets.body: Citi reiterates Buy on Dell, highlighting $61B AI orders in Q2 with a $95B backlog and pipeline running multiples of backlog. Enterprise AI customer base grew 60% in six months to 6,500+, yet only 10-15% of enterprises have completed meaningful agentic AI modernization. Supply constraints (DRAM, NAND, optics) expected to tighten further, with customers now planning 2-4 years ahead. RBC separately initiates DELL at Outperform with $640 PT (26% upside).

bullets.title: CSCO: Citi Buy ($139 PT, +29%); $7.5B FY27 AI Revenue Target, Campus Refresh Cycle Just Starting
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on Cisco with $139 PT, citing $9B+ AI orders in FY26 and a $7.5B AI revenue target for FY27 (60% Silicon One systems, 40% Acacia optics). Campus refresh driven by first-ever Catalyst 4K/6K end-of-life dates; total networking TAM framed at $100B+. Q1 FY27 expected to be gross margin trough as hyperscaler hardware mix is high; improvement expected as software subscriptions attach. Silicon One currently <10% of switches but expected majority by FY29. New Supermicro partnership for end-to-end AI factory deals.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Citi Buy ($447 PT) — GenAI Search Drives Higher-Intent Traffic, Better Conversions, Cloud Reaccelerating
bullets.body: Citi is incrementally positive on Google search advertising: AI queries average 20+ keywords vs. 2-3 in traditional search, targeting higher-intent users with better conversion rates and a shorter path to purchase. Google Cloud revenue is reaccelerating on TPU and Gemini demand. Citi maintains Buy at $447 PT (~28x 2027E GAAP EPS of $15.72).

bullets.title: CRWD: Citi Buy ($260 PT, 24.5% upside) — AI-Native Products, Flex-First GTM, ~25% Revenue CAGR Target
bullets.body: CrowdStrike at Citi's TMT Conference highlighted new AI-native security products (SafeMind, Guardion) and a Flex-first go-to-market motion. Management expects agentic AI to durably increase security urgency. Guardian (AIDR) is positioned to be larger than EDR. Flex eliminates revenue cliff risk. Citi targets ~25% topline CAGR with >30% FCF margins; $260 PT implies 24.5% upside.

bullets.title: META: Wells Fargo Upgrades to Overweight, PT $640→$820; JPM Also Upgraded on AI Agents
bullets.body: Wells Fargo upgraded Meta to Overweight from Equal Weight, raising PT from $640 to $820, citing early-stage frontier AI models and product opportunities beyond advertising. JPMorgan separately upgraded META to Overweight based on Models Agents deployment. Hedgeye also demonstrated Meta's Muse agent completing a live Shopify purchase, though reliability issues remain (mis-filled address, payment flow constraints).

bullets.title: SHOP: Bernstein Initiates Outperform at $160 PT; Agentic Commerce Emerging Catalyst
bullets.body: Bernstein initiated Shopify at Outperform with a $160 PT (26% upside from $126.60; FactSet consensus $172.67). Separately, Hedgeye's live test of Meta's Muse agent completing a Shopify merchant purchase highlights agentic commerce as an emerging catalyst/risk for Shopify's checkout ecosystem, with Shop Pay currently bypassed in agent flows due to a single technical constraint.

bullets.title: NVDA: DOJ Investigating Groq Licensing Deal for Potential Antitrust Evasion
bullets.body: The DOJ is investigating Nvidia's licensing deal with Groq, allegedly structured to avoid antitrust scrutiny. Separately, DeepSeek launched a significantly lower-cost AI model that pressured memory-related semis broadly. The tech sector was down 0.94% on the day with semis down 2.7%.

bullets.title: CRM: UBS Neutral ($240 PT) on Claudeforce — Narrative Shift, Not Material Numbers; Listen Labs M&A Reported
bullets.body: UBS maintains Neutral on Salesforce at $240 PT (13x CY27E EV/FCF), saying the Claudeforce (Anthropic partnership) drove a 20%+ stock move on narrative shift rather than material revenue uplift, with the first plugin only in limited pilot. Separately, CRM is reportedly in talks to acquire AI startup Listen Labs for $2.55B.

bullets.title: SNOW: Citi Buy ($490 PT, 47.8% upside) — AI SKUs Early-Stage but Expanding; Open Architecture Key Differentiator
bullets.body: Citi hosted Snowflake CFO at its TMT Conference and maintains Buy at $490 PT (19x FY2029E EV/revenue, 61x FY2029E EV/FCF). AI SKUs (CoCo, CoWork, Cortex) are early-stage but driving incremental usage by expanding beyond traditional data teams. Management differentiates on open architecture, Iceberg-based data access, and multi-model/multi-cloud flexibility versus closed ecosystems.

bullets.title: MDB: Goldman Conference — Atlas Deepening Enterprise Penetration; AI Inflection Expected as Workloads Scale
bullets.body: MongoDB management highlighted durable Atlas growth from deeper enterprise penetration, vector search cross-sell, and self-managed Enterprise Advanced as a second growth driver (double-digit expected growth). AI demand is building but early; the company is building AI-assisted migration tooling to compress migration timelines. Voyage acquisition pairs embedding models with MongoDB's operational capabilities.

bullets.title: INTU: Goldman Conference — FY27 Is Investment Year; AI Embedded in Core, Not Sold Separately
bullets.body: Intuit positioned FY27 as an investment year to rebuild new-customer acquisition while scaling faster-growing initiatives, targeting durable double-digit revenue and high-teens EPS growth. Consumer tax revenue faces near-term pressure as pricing becomes more competitive for lower-income filers, but the strategy bets on higher lifetime value via Credit Karma cross-sell. AI is embedded in core workflows rather than sold as a separate feature; near-term focus on adoption and repeat usage before monetization.

bullets.title: NXST: Operating Ahead of Plan; FCC Deregulation is Key M&A Catalyst; Digital to Surpass National Ads in 2026
bullets.body: Nexstar at Goldman's conference reported operating performance ahead of EBITDA and FCF outlook, with political advertising stronger than expected. Digital revenue expected to surpass national advertising revenue in 2026. FCC deregulation of ownership rules viewed as the major catalyst for accretive M&A and industry consolidation; Tegna legal restrictions resolution is top priority. Core ad trends soft, guided to mid-single-digit non-political decline in Q3.

bullets.title: T: AT&T Reiterates Double-Digit EPS Growth; Fiber + 5G Converged Household Strategy Driving Acceleration
bullets.body: AT&T at BofA conference reiterated its three-year double-digit EPS growth outlook and $45B shareholder return target. Broadband growth expected to accelerate via Lumen footprint, fiber expansion, and fixed wireless. Converged households targeted for higher lifetime value; 50% broadband-wireless convergence targeted. iPhone 18 Pro subsidies rose to $1,200 (from $1,100) matching Apple's price increase but remain rational per JPMorgan.

bullets.title: STX: HAMR Volume Crossover by Dec 2026; 70%+ Incremental Gross Margins; Capital Return Shifting to Buybacks in 2027
bullets.body: Seagate at Goldman's conference guided that HAMR drives (30TB shipping broadly, 40TB to top hyperscalers, 50TB by end-2027) will reach volume crossover by December 2026. Incremental gross margins have been running above 70% and are expected to persist for several quarters. Capital allocation shifts toward share repurchases in 2027 after debt reduction. Main downside risk is data-center buildout delays, not demand elimination.

bullets.title: FOXA: Goldman Conference Positive; Roku Acquisition on Track H1 2027; FY27 Momentum Continuing
bullets.body: Fox Corp indicated ongoing momentum in FY27 following a record FY26 from strong upfront, ad pricing/volume gains, and Tubi performance. The Roku takeover remains its top priority, expected to close H1 2027 despite DOJ examination. Fox expects a major political advertising tailwind next year and has a secure sports portfolio. FOXA was +2.1% on the session.

bullets.title: MSFT: Plans to Triple Data Center Capacity from 12GW to 38GW by 2032 to Support AI/Cloud
bullets.body: Microsoft plans to expand data center capacity from 12GW to 38GW by 2032, driven by AI and cloud business demand growth, per a Bloomberg report. Separately, an MSFT EMEA non-deal roadshow is scheduled September 14-17 in Stockholm, Zurich, and London.
